tasks.short: Prepare and deliver language and culture lectures

steps.what: Select lecture aims, language examples and cultural sources for the student level
Prepare lecture explanations and examples from the selected sources

loop.purpose: Draft level-appropriate explanations from lecturer-selected sources
loop.input: Lecture brief, exact examples and cultural source passages
loop.check: Lecturer checks grammar, idiom, register, cultural nuance and student-level suitability
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unreliable language or cultural content returns to manual preparation
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates do not adapt conceptual explanations to the particular language and student level

steps.what: Check the lecture, deliver it and respond to student language and cultural questions

tasks.design: Use reusable lecture structures in {DOCS} first, then bounded drafting for explanatory prose. The lecturer checks linguistic and cultural meaning and retains live delivery, pronunciation or signing demonstrations and student interaction.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparation includes repeated explanatory wording as well as substantive teaching choices.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting can propose editable explanations from an explicit teaching brief.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising subtle register errors, stereotypes and misleading simplifications.
tasks.human_edge: Teach the language in context and respond to learners.
tasks.altitude: A small reduction in wording preparation; live teaching remains unchanged.

evidence.claim: EduGenAI offers a teaching chat platform, not demonstrated accuracy for every language or cultural context.
Lecture preparation savings are unmeasured and depend on independent language checking.

assumptions: Boundary covers lecture-specific preparation and delivery, excluding separately counted handout production or assessment.

Lecturer captures language, level, learning aim, approved examples, register and exact cultural source passages/versions in s1. Capture remains counted; absent reliable support triggers manual preparation.
Student questions arise during s3, not as advance model inputs. Signing, pronunciation and live interaction remain human without assumed synthetic demonstrations.
Test native DOCS templates first; use the loop only where the lecturer can independently verify language and context.
unknowns: Language, student level and model reliability for the subject
research_questions: Can checked drafts reduce preparation without flattening linguistic and cultural nuance?

already_counted.description: Draft review, final check and live teaching

incremental.description: Maintain examples and inspect recurring language errors

approvals.approved_version: Exact prepared lecture and source versions; revisions require recheck. Live explanations and answers remain lecturer authored

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R94 gives6 gross minus4 upkeep=2 net. Unreliable language drafts may be discarded; repeated familiar explanations may yield1%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Research and publish language and literature findings

steps.what: Conduct research through source study, analysis and original scholarly interpretation
Write and publish findings in scholarly journals, books or electronic media

tasks.design: Retain original interpretation and scholarly writing in {DOCS}. No administrative baseline or automatic argument generation is assumed within this research task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research contribution depends on original interpretation and defensible evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: General drafting capability does not establish replacement of scholarly reasoning.
tasks.still_hard: Developing an original claim and addressing contrary readings.
tasks.human_edge: Create and defend a contribution to knowledge.
tasks.altitude: Research and author responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Compare textual interpretations without erasing context

evidence.claim: The supplied teaching capabilities do not establish replacement of original language and literature scholarship.

assumptions: Boundary covers the scholar's research, writing and publication actions; publisher review and production labour are outside and unchanged.
Lecturer produces findings during s1 and checks argument, source references and final text during s2. No structured valid-argument or publication-ready flag is assumed.
Test existing reference and document functions before additions; no new system is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no new software or process is introduced.
research_questions: Which parts of the argument depend on primary source interpretation?

already_counted.description: Scholarly writing, source check and author acceptance

approvals.approved_version: Exact manuscript and source versions; any edit requires renewed author acceptance before publication

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives zero gross and net. Interpretive and empirical scholarship both retain research and author work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep current with language and literature developments

steps.what: Read current literature, talk with colleagues and participate in professional organizations and activities

tasks.design: Retain critical reading and professional participation. Summaries in {DOCS} may orient the lecturer but do not substitute for understanding the underlying scholarship.
tasks.previous_blocker: Professional learning requires engagement with nuanced language and arguments.
tasks.enabler_now: Topic summaries do not demonstrate equivalent professional understanding.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising important conceptual changes and evaluating unfamiliar approaches.
tasks.human_edge: Integrate scholarship with teaching and research judgment.

reach.learn: Evaluate methods beyond the lecturer's specialism

evidence.claim: Scopus AI provides topic summaries and foundational papers; this does not establish replacement of critical reading or professional participation.

assumptions: Boundary is substantive professional learning, excluding separate catalogue maintenance.
Scholars and colleagues produce source contributions; the lecturer evaluates them during s1. No structured importance or correctness score is assumed.
Test existing research access before additions; no change is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no new system or process is introduced.
research_questions: Which developments require full reading to understand their significance?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives zero gross and net. Familiar and unfamiliar literature both retain critical learning.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile, administer and grade language examinations

steps.what: Compile examinations and define answer keys and language assessment rubrics
Check the examination, administer written or oral tasks and capture candidate responses
Mark closed language questions against explicitly allowed responses
Judge open and oral work, check proposed scores and accept examination grades

tasks.design: Configure exact closed-question marking in the {LMS}. Retain examiner judgment for expression, interpretation, oral language and signing, including all final score checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Some examinations mix mechanical fixed-answer scoring with contextual language judgments.
tasks.enabler_now: Native assessment keys can produce proposals for explicitly closed responses.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising valid alternate expressions and assessing communicative effectiveness.
tasks.human_edge: Judge language meaning and fair assessment.
tasks.altitude: Less fixed-answer scoring; examiner authority remains unchanged.

reach.learn: Distinguish exact-response tasks from contextual expression

evidence.claim: Ans automatically marks closed questions and supports open-question marking distribution.
Language examination effort and savings are an unmeasured mixed-exam scenario.

assumptions: Boundary covers examination preparation through grade acceptance, excluding official record transfer and coursework grading.

Lecturer captures item/version, exact allowed responses, case or accent handling, score weights and rubric in s1. No approximate semantic matching is assumed; unlisted plausible expressions return to examiner review.

Candidate roster comes from existing registry work; lecturer associates responses with candidate ids during s2. Oral and signed responses are observed and noted in s2 without assumed recordings; all their judgment time stays in s4.
Test native closed-question marking first. This split assumes15% baseline mechanical marking; wholly expressive or already automatically scored examinations yield no additional saving.
unknowns: Exam formats, allowed response variation and current automatic marking
research_questions: Can exact keys preserve valid language variation without increasing examiner correction time?

already_counted.description: Administration, open and oral judgment and final score checks

incremental.description: Maintain exact response keys and inspect scoring exceptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact examination package, item versions, keys and rubric; changes require renewed check
Exact candidate responses, rubric, score proposals and grade set; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R85 gives15 gross minus6 upkeep=9 net. Wholly open or already automatically scored examinations yield zero; mixed manual scoring may yield3%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Limited support for lecture wording and closed scoring; language teaching, scholarship and assessment judgment remain human.
reach: Work with teaching assistants on language variation and rubrics
role.ambitious_version: A language lecturer who uses preparation support while preserving contextual teaching and scholarly interpretation.

job.title: Foreign Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary
